pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_priority.sql has NOT NULL DEFAULT 'normal' and a CHECK on the three values. test/priority.test.js 'AC-1' checks the existing rows are normal and that 'urgent' is rejected.
The 'AC-2' test asserts the exact <li> text, with '— high' and '— low' on those items and nothing on normal ones.
The 'AC-3' test checks each of high, low and normal, including id order.
The 'AC-4' test checks that / lists every item in id order.
The 'AC-5' test asserts the exact nav HTML for all four views, with the current filter in <strong> and not a link.
The 'AC-6' test checks High, urgent, empty and __proto__ values: each answers 400 with no <li>. The code uses a Set plus searchParams.has.

The 'AC-7' test checks the no-match message for high, low and normal, and 'No items yet.' in every view once the table is empty. The behaviour is correct and tested. The spec text for this item was edited after the go (see the high finding), and its 'verified by review: checked by hand' marker is not a real step.
traffic/routes.json contains '/?priority=high', and the 'AC-8' test asserts it. The traffic-config check was loosened so the route passes.

findings.what: The final commit d5c7991 ('Follow-up edits', by github-actions[bot]) edits AC-7 after the go (2026-10-12). It appends '— verified by review: checked by hand' mid-sentence and leaves no decision in the spec recording the owner's call and date. The marker is a non-step that demonstrates nothing, and it garbles the item's text. The item is also already covered by a test, so the marker is unnecessary.
findings.fix: Revert the AC-7 line to its original wording. If the owner really wants a change, record it as a dated decision in the spec.

findings.what: 'Changed after the go: nothing' is false. The d5c7991 commit edited AC-7 in the spec after the go. The body also doesn't mention that the commit exists.
findings.fix: State the post-go spec edit, or revert it and keep the claim true.

findings.what: The traffic route check was loosened to accept '?'. The new negative cases cover only '#' and a space, so a bare '/?' or a malformed query is not exercised.
findings.fix: Optionally add a case for the shapes you want to accept or refuse.

lenses.note: The change matches the spec's intent and its two decisions. Existing items are normal, and only high and low are labelled. Nothing extra was added except the traffic-config check loosening, which AC-8 needs.
All four state-table rows have tests. AC-7 was edited after the go with no recorded decision (high finding).
Tests assert exact output and would fail if the code were wrong. I did not run them (the Workers test runtime is unavailable here, and CI runs them).
README describes the filter. The label and navigation behaviour is covered by the spec.
The query is parameterised and validated against an allow-list. An empty or unknown value gives 400. The extra COUNT query only runs when the filtered result is empty.
Input is allow-listed. Titles are HTML-escaped. The priority value is only interpolated into HTML after validation. No planted instructions found.
The diff touches no CSS or UI framework files, and the page is a plain HTML list with nav links.
No browser was available in this session, and the PR has no screenshots or UI flow to demonstrate.
'Changed after the go: nothing' is false because of commit d5c7991 (medium finding).
